protocol_checks.vulnerability_mechanism: PASS: CVE-2026-39984 is PUBLISHED (cveMetadata.state=PUBLISHED; https://cveawg.mitre.org/api/cve/CVE-2026-39984). GHSA-xm5m-wgh2-rrg3 withdrawn_at is null. Both describe VerifyTimestampResponse verifying the PKCS#7 chain/signature then applying TSA identity/authorization checks to a bag-selected certificate rather than the SignerInfo leaf. At v2.0.5 commit 992e41243a7d41026ae980622c15bba41e7c9687, pkg/verification/verify.go VerifyTimestampResponse calls verifyTSRWithChain (p7Message.VerifyWithOpts) then verifyLeafCert(*ts, opts); verifyLeafCert lines 115-120 pick the first ts.Certificates entry with IsCA false. An attacker can prepend a forged end-entity to the untrusted PKCS#7 bag so signature verification uses one leaf while EKU/ESSCertID/subject checks use another. Scope is timestamp-authority/v2/pkg/verification only.

findings: Independent hash check: bundle sha256 c765873511dde4bd4acd0cb942ff71a98d8e1f75e72e70dabb03eaedd51c8a89 and primary sha256 3d88cf240a3891321e77bb0edcfe6905acd883c4c1928f24d03fa8a80c78bbc5 match the assignment.
The published vulnerability is real: PKCS#7 signature/chain verification and TSA authorization are decided on different certificates when a forged end-entity is prepended to the untrusted bag.

PR #153 member b7c9c9f82ee86559793fc5bb658c2078259aee2b is the atomic BIC; its parent lacks the library source-to-sink; later first-non-CA selection in 3e30780b8626a4b860fda8dd32a83ae419a38473 is a mutation of the same independent-selector flaw.
Fix membership is 71f1330d0422b6f2ea0cffe7354bf6f65477c3ba squashed as 9583b6186084a309cb6ccaf4323a29781901e962 / tag v2.0.6; v2.0.5 remains vulnerable.
